name: Pettneu am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful alternative to St. Anton with direct access to the Arlberg ski area and the charming old town center.
beschreibung:
Overview

Pettneu am Arlberg is situated in the sunny Stanzer Valley in the Tyrolean district of Landeck at an altitude of 1,222 metres, just six kilometres east of the world-famous ski resort of St. Anton am Arlberg. The municipality covers 56.8 square kilometres along the Rosanna mountain river and comprises the main village of Pettneu along with the picturesque neighbouring hamlet of Schnann. Home to approximately 1,500 permanent residents, Pettneu is widely regarded as the authentic, family-friendly, and peaceful counterpart to bustling St. Anton. The valley is flanked to the north by the jagged limestone crags of the Lechtal Alps and to the south by the glaciated Verwall Group, dominated by Mount Hoher Riffler – at 3,168 metres the highest peak in the entire Verwall Range. The village has lovingly preserved its rural charm, featuring Engadine-style stone houses, baroque churches, and exceptional year-round alpine outdoor recreation.

History

The settlement was first recorded in historical documents around 1300 under the name Pudnew. The name derives from the Rhaeto-Romanic ponte novu, meaning new bridge – a clear reference to the historic river crossing over the rushing Rosanna along the ancient Arlberg trade route. In 1386, Tyrolean sovereign Duke Leopold III endowed an independent chaplaincy, and archaeological excavations in 1992 revealed Romanesque foundations beneath the Gothic nave. A prominent artistic landmark is the Parish Church of the Assumption of Mary: this 15th-century Gothic church was redesigned in Baroque style in 1716 and embellished in 1759 by renowned painter Anton Kirchebner with monumental ceiling frescoes depicting the Coronation and Visitation of the Virgin. A singular cultural heritage survives in Schnann: the historic bell forge of the Scherl family, where traditional cattle bells have been hand-hammered and brass-plated since 1703; master smith Walter Scherl is recognized as Austria's last active livestock bell maker.

Getting There

Pettneu am Arlberg benefits from direct access via the major Arlberg transport corridor. Motorists travel via the four-lane S16 Arlberg Expressway, taking the dedicated exit for Pettneu am Arlberg or Schnann; this stretch is covered by the standard Austrian motorway vignette without special tunnel tolls unless entering Vorarlberg. Rail travellers arrive at the international express station of St. Anton am Arlberg (just six kilometres away) or Landeck-Zams station, both served regularly by international Railjet, EuroCity, and ICE trains. From St. Anton station forecourt, modern VVT regional bus route 4242 operates frequently directly into Pettneu and Schnann. During the winter season, frequent complimentary ski shuttles whisk winter sports enthusiasts directly to the base gondolas of St. Anton am Arlberg.

Tips

A natural marvel not to be missed is the Schnann Gorge (Schnanner Klamm): secure timber walkways and bridges wind through the sheer chasm alongside thundering waterfalls, passing a dedicated rock-climbing crag featuring 42 sport climbing routes. Experienced mountaineers can undertake the demanding alpine ascent of Mount Hoher Riffler (3,168 m), which commands sweeping 360-degree panoramas extending into the Swiss Alps. The Edmund Graf Hut at 2,375 metres in the idyllic Malfontal valley serves as a classic mountain refuge and hiking destination. For rejuvenation, the Wellnesspark Arlberg Stanzertal offers an indoor pool, extensive sauna suites, and relaxation lawns. In winter, cross-country skiers can join the 40-kilometre snow-sure Stanzer Valley Trail right from the village, while downhill skiers access over 300 kilometres of slopes in the Ski Arlberg arena within minutes.
